messages.subject: sample size
messages.body_plain:
We would like to implement the sample size estimation in the lab for DDA and SRM data. We have followed the example case published in Surinova et al., 2015 and we understand that MSstats simulates our experimental data, with different number of proteins and samples to predict a model that will be used to calculate the accuracy for a specific number of samples and FC.

Still, we have some opened questions that we would like to troubleshoot with you, if possible.

1- Is it correct to use “equalizeMedians” as normalization in 'dataProcess' function for SRM data? We found a brief description in the Surinova paper, but we did not understand the details about the calculation. Is it possible to explain how the medians are equalized?

2- In the case of SRM labeled based experiments, does MSstats (by default) normalize the light intensities by the heavy intensities of the corresponding peptides, without any additional action?

3- What does the “LogIntensities” column in the “RunLevelData” (generated by 'dataProcess' function) stand for? Is it the Log2heavy intensity-Log2light intensity?

4- We noticed that the output in “ComparisonResult” file seems to be not used for the prediction of sample size, is it correct?

5- What number of biological samples do you suggest we should use for sample size estimation, in case of DDA and SRM, for cell culture-based and clinical proteomics assays?

To make the questions clearer,  we have attached the input file and the results.

Thank you very much. Best, Daniela

messages.subject: Re: sample size
messages.body_plain:
1 and 2. If you have SRM with heavy isotope labeled peptide, yes, we recommend using equalized median method. There is the explanation in MSstats user manual : http://msstats.org/msstats-2/

3. It is summarized log2 light intensity.

4. Sample size is calculated with estimated variation from the linear mixed model.

5. there is no one answer for that. MSstats used the data as a pilot study and assumed that variation in next study would be similar as those in the pilot study. I recommend at least 3 replicates per group.

HTH
- Meena

messages.subject: MaxQtoMSstatsFormat error
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to convert MaxQuant data to MSstats format following the 2017 published guide. I have all three input files set up as suggested by the tutorial, but when I run quant <- MaxQtoMSstatsFormat(evidence=infile, annotation=annot, proteinGroups=proteinGroups) I get the error message: Error in dim(ordered) <- ns : dims [product 1] do not match the length of object [0]. I believe my annotation file is formatted correctly based on the examples on Github, so I can't figure out why the data will not convert/combine correctly. Do you have any suggestions to fix this error or ideas what I might be doing wrong?

Thank you,

Annelise

messages.subject: MSStats TMT normalization / imputation
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using the latest version of msstats-TMT for an experiment, consisting of 3 batches, each batch with 2 normalization channels (4 genotypes spread over 3 batches, 8 channels in each batch used for real samples, rest used for normalization or left empty).

I have compared the settings "method = "msstats", normalization = TRUE, MBimpute = TRUE" vs "method = "msstats", normalization = TRUE, MBimpute = FALSE". I now have two questions:
a) MBimpute = TRUE" and  MBimpute = FALSE yield the same number of proteins (3580) that were quantified in all three batches. Shouldn't imputation increase that number?

b) the box-and-whisker plot of the "normalized" data looks a bit diverse (see attached). Shouldn't the various channels have very similar overall intensities after normalization?

Thanks for any support!

Oliver

messages.subject: Re: MSStats TMT normalization / imputation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Oliver,

a) MBimpute = TRUE and  MBimpute = FALSE may give the same number of proteins. Because MSstatsTMT imputes the missing values for each spectrum within a run. So if your TMT data has a low percentage of missing values within a run (such as <2%), then the imputation possibly doesn't change the number of proteins.

b) MSstatsTMT 1.2.5 (Bioconductor version) performs one step reference channel-based normalization. For each protein, it equalizes the protein intensities of the reference channel across runs to their median and then applies the same shift to other channels in the corresponding run. It doesn't adjust the protein intensity ranges in different channels within a run. But we are going to add a global median normalization to MSstatsTMT, which makes the overall intensities similar across channels and runs. This new function will be released in one or two weeks. If you would like to try it now, the code is already available in Github https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsTMT.

Best,
Ting
